prerequisites: Laws of thermodynamics, application of balance equations, fluid dynamics, fundamentals of electrical engineering

learning_outcomes.text: Analyze energy technology issues holistically, systematically, and quantitatively under technical, economic, and climate aspects.
Describe, quantify, and calculate energy yields for energy technology plants and systems using energy flow diagrams, describing all relevant energy flows formulaically.
Know and apply efficiencies and utilization rates for various energy conversion technologies to describe, analyze, and compare cascaded or coupled systems.

Understand the mechanisms of action and loss in energy conversion processes, and thereby evaluate and compare conversion concepts or energy generation plants based on metrics such as energy density, resource input/area requirement, and CO2 intensity, and estimate potential future.

Know the fundamentals of transport and transmission of heat, electrical energy, and chemical energy (gas) and estimate or calculate losses and other transport properties, and thereby analyze and evaluate various energy distribution concepts.

Recognize the problem of electrical energy storage and its importance for grid stability, classify storage concepts based on fundamental storage characteristics, identify sensible areas of application, and develop solution concepts.

Economically analyze energy technology plants and systems by applying financial mathematical methods and formulas, calculating profitability and costs, and justifying investment decisions and pricing.

Recognize, qualitatively estimate, and forecast the influence of external events and energy policy decisions on energy prices through their learned understanding of market-based price formation mechanisms.

Roughly dimension energy technology plants in a professional environment and systematically techno-economically evaluate energy technology concepts, and furthermore, as an engineer, contribute to a factual and evidence-based discussion in the energy policy context.

syllabus_topics: Motivation: connection between energy and climate problems, societal importance of energy technology, climate neutrality
Connection between energy conversion and CO2 emissions, technology-specific emission factors
Fundamentals: balance equations, concept of exergy and anergy, types of heat transfer, energy technology and energy economics terms
Concept of energy flow diagrams: creation and application for generic balance-like description of energy conversion processes

Mechanisms of action, conversion efficiencies, operating characteristics, and rough design/dimensioning of the most relevant CO2-minimal energy conversion technologies (according to IPCC AR5 life cycle emissions), e.g.:
Solar energy conversion (photovoltaic and solar thermal)
Grid-bound energy transport of heat, electricity, and gas: description of transport properties, components, approximate quantification of transport losses
Storage problem with focus on electrical energy: power balance equation, storage options and storage properties, areas of application
Economic evaluation of energy generation plants: investment cost calculation, levelized cost of electricity
Pricing and trading of energy: energy exchange, merit-order principle, price components for end consumers
Evaluation, discussion of current energy policy topics
assessment_rules: Students can choose between a 90-minute written exam or a 20-minute oral exam. The specific examination format will be announced at the beginning of the course.
